newsitem.title: USA: U.S. seeking details of Turkey-Iran pipeline deal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. seeking details of Turkey-Iran pipeline deal.

text.p: The United States said on Friday it was seeking details of a contract awarded by Turkey this week for part of a natural gas pipeline link with Iran to see if the agreement violated U.S. law.

Turkey's state-run pipeline company Botas said on Monday it had awarded a $118 million contract to the Turkish consortium Fernas-STFA ENERKOM to build a section of the pipeline between the Eastern Turkish town of Erzurum and the Iranian border.

"We've been in close touch with the Turkish government to determine the details of the announcement so that we can determine whether or not this action and other actions would constitute any kind of a violation of the Iran-Libya Sanctions Act," a State Department spokesman said.

"The United States has not determined that this particular action or any other by the government of Turkey would trigger sanctions under the Iran-Libya act," the spokesman, Nicholas Burns, told a news briefing.
"We will continue to look at this issue and will keep it under review," he added.

This week's contract is part of a $23 billion 23-year gas supply deal signed by Turkey and Iran in August 1996 under which a pipeline is to be constructed from the Iranian city of Tabriz to the Turkish capital Ankara.

Last year's Iran-Libya Sanctions Act gave President Bill Clinton authority to impose economic sanctions on any company that invested in the oil or gas sector of those two countries, accused by Washington of sponsoring terrorism.
